Hey, I would like to answer this for you. I work prodominantly with sapce optics and robotics and know exactly what this effect is.

The picture on the right was taken from a very high orbit (my guess is geosynchronous) so the horizon is very close to the "sides/top/bottom" of the earth, this is a true representation as most think of it.

The left picture was taken from LEO. This is closer to the surface so the horizon is a lot closer, hence, less of the geography is visible (kinda like standing on mountain will give a nice view but not a view of the whole hemisphere you're on). Now, when this close to the planet, it fills a huge field of view so they used a fish-eye lense to make it seem like a ball with a smaller angular width.

As a side note for space conspiracies that use different images of the same thing to draw conclusions, unless the exact same optics were used, its virtually impossible to draw parrellels.
